summary: Iteration 6 (Northstar GRC) — Session invalidation on password reset. Added /app/backend/tests/test_iteration6.py (2 test items covering 8 acceptance criteria in one end-to-end flow + a final-state check). Cumulative pytest serial: 82/82 passing (2 new iter6 + 80 iter1-5). Verified full flow: (1) contributor login -> pre-reset JWT works on /api/auth/me; (2) synthetic OAuth session row inserted in db.sessions with session_token 'sess_iter6_<hex>' -> Authorization: Bearer <session_token> returns 200 on /api/auth/me BEFORE reset; (3) issued fresh reset token (secrets.token_urlsafe(32) + sha256 into password_resets, 1h exp); (4) POST /api/auth/reset-password returns 200 with response shape {ok:true, sessions_revoked:<int>} and sessions_revoked>=1 (matches our synthetic row); (5) db.users doc for contributor now has ISO-parseable password_changed_at; (6) db.sessions row is gone (verified via direct find_one); (7) same Bearer <session_token> now returns 401 on /api/auth/me AFTER reset; (8) the pre-reset JWT now returns 401 on /api/auth/me (because JWT iat < user.password_changed_at); (9) fresh login with the new password returns 200 with a new access_token that survives repeated /api/auth/me calls. Regression: iter5 test that asserted r.json()=={ok:true} was updated to match new contract {ok:true, sessions_revoked:int}. Contributor password restored to TEST_ONLY_PASSWORD with bcrypt.hashpw AND password_changed_at $unset in the test teardown (verified via 200 login). All iter1-5 regressions (auth, dashboard, calendar, bulk incl. set-due-date, board PDF, notifications, exceptions CRUD, evidence) still green serially.

minor.issue: Under parallel xdist -n2 --dist loadscope, backend_test.py's module-scoped contributor JWT (minted at module import on worker A) can be invalidated mid-run when iter6 (on worker B) sets password_changed_at on acme-contributor@example.test, causing TestClients::test_contributor_scoped_to_acme and iter5 bulk tests to see 401 during the ~4-8s window before iter6's teardown $unsets password_changed_at. Serial (-n 0) passes 82/82. Consider: (a) function-scoped auth tokens in shared test modules, or (b) a cross-worker file lock, or (c) a dedicated 'ephemeral' seeded user for iter6 that no other test uses.

action_items: (nit) In server.py _get_user_from_token, iat is a datetime object when encoded by pyjwt but pyjwt actually encodes datetime -> integer seconds; on decode it's an int, and the code correctly uses datetime.fromtimestamp(int(iat), tz=utc). Verified working. Consider also honouring iat_dt <= pca_dt (equal timestamps at 1-second resolution) — current strict '<' could theoretically leave a same-second token valid; not exploitable in practice but tighten to '<=' for defense-in-depth.

(carry-over from iter5 review) /api/auth/reset-password now correctly stamps password_changed_at and revokes db.sessions rows — resolved. Still add a unique index on password_resets.token_hash and invalidate prior unused reset tokens for the same user when a new one is issued.
(carry-over) server.py grew to 1718 lines — extract auth-recovery / bulk / calendar / board-report modules.
(carry-over) CORSMiddleware allow_origins=['*'] + allow_credentials=False still contradicts login Set-Cookie flow.
(test-infra) Consider a dedicated ephemeral user for future security-sensitive tests to avoid cross-worker JWT invalidation races.
critical_code_review_comments: create_access_token now includes 'iat' (datetime with tz) — pyjwt serialises to int seconds; on decode payload['iat'] is int; _get_user_from_token converts via datetime.fromtimestamp(int(iat), tz=timezone.utc) — correct.
password_changed_at stored as ISO string via _now(); parsing tolerates both str and datetime and normalises to UTC. Good defensive parsing.
reset_password_endpoint invalidates ALL sessions for the user_id (not scoped to a device/session) — matches OWASP guidance for password-reset flow.
Response contract expanded to include sessions_revoked:int. Existing test that asserted exact-equal shape was updated. Any external client of this API should be told it may now include extra keys.
The 'iat < password_changed_at' JWT rejection is correctly placed BEFORE returning the user, so downstream handlers never see an old token.
OAuth session invalidation currently relies only on db.sessions deletion; if there's any in-memory session cache elsewhere it would need to be invalidated too (none observed in server.py).

success_rate.backend: 100% serial (82/82); 99% parallel (81/82 with 1 test-infra race, functionality verified correct)

test_credentials: See /app/memory/test_credentials.md. Used acme-contributor@example.test/TEST_ONLY_PASSWORD (temporarily TEST_ONLY_RESET_PASSWORD during test; RESTORED to TEST_ONLY_PASSWORD and password_changed_at $unset — verified with 200 login in test_restore_state_final).
seed_data_creation: Iter6 inserts one password_resets row (marked used=true after test) and one db.sessions row (deleted by the /reset-password endpoint under test). Both are per-test-run and self-cleaning.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter6 shipped: (1) create_access_token now embeds iat; (2) _get_user_from_token rejects JWTs with iat < user.password_changed_at (ISO string in db); (3) /api/auth/reset-password sets users.password_changed_at=<ISO now> AND does db.sessions.delete_many({user_id: rec.user_id}); (4) response shape is {ok:true, sessions_revoked:int}. The /api/auth/me helper accepts Authorization: Bearer <token> and internally routes to _get_user_from_token (JWT) OR falls back to _get_user_from_session (matches db.sessions.session_token) — so an inserted db.sessions row with matching session_token works as a bearer session. Cumulative pytest: 82. Known test-infra parallel race: iter6's password_changed_at write invalidates module-scope JWTs held by backend_test.py/iter5 on other xdist workers during a ~4-8s window; use -n 0 for the definitive signal or convert affected fixtures to function-scoped. Restore snippet remains: bcrypt.hashpw(b'TEST_ONLY_PASSWORD', bcrypt.gensalt()) + $unset password_changed_at.
rca of the issue: N/A — no functional bugs found; iteration 6 requirements fully met. One iter5 test needed a contract update (assert r.json()=={ok:true} -> assert response contains ok+sessions_revoked); one parallel-mode test-infra race is documented as a minor issue, does not indicate a product bug (serial run is 82/82 pass and confirms all iter1-6 behaviour).
